title: Shared decision-making in rare hematological and oncological diseases - system-wide implementation
summary:
The PELIKAN-FLUG study investigates how people with rare blood disorders can be better supported in making medical decisions. These diseases are rare and treatment often involves complex choices with different benefits and risks. Many patients therefore wish for more understandable information and support when deciding together with their healthcare professionals.

The aim of the study is to examine whether a digital decision aid helps patients feel better informed, more confident, and more actively involved in treatment decisions. In addition, the study explores how such support tools can be integrated into routine healthcare.

Adults with selected rare blood disorders can take part. The decision aid is provided via hospitals, medical practices, and patient organisations. Participants complete short questionnaires before using the decision aid, immediately afterwards, and again after three and six months to assess changes in patient empowerment, knowledge, decisional conflict, and participation in decision-making.

interventions.name: This is a single-arm, intraindividual pre–post study design with follow-up assessments: adult patients diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis, post-essential thrombocythemia (post-ET) myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera (post-PV) myelofibrosis, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, or acquired aplast

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosis of primary myelofibrosis or post-ET/PV myelofibrosis
• or: diagnosis of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
• or: diagnosis of acquired aplastic anemia
Exclusion criteria:
• language barrier
